title: Why Bats Hang Upside Down for 20 Hours a Day 🦇
description:
Why do bats sleep upside down? Bats can't take off from the ground like birds, so they hang high up by their toes, let go and drop straight into flight, while a tendon lock in their feet keeps them hanging with zero muscle effort.

topic: Why do bats sleep upside down?
script:
You'd pass out sleeping upside down,
but some bats do it 20 hours a day.
So why hang like that?
Bats have a takeoff problem.
They're the only mammals that truly fly,
but their wings can't lift them off the ground,
and their back legs are too tiny to run.
So they sleep up high, hanging by their toes.
Time to go?
They let go, drop,
and they're flying before they hit anything.
But doesn't hanging all day get tiring?
Nope.
Their toe tendons work like a locking clip.
Body weight pulls the tendon tight,
and the claws clamp shut, with zero effort.
To let go, they use muscles to open them.
And the blood rush to the head?
Bats are so light, it barely happens.
Plus, up high, most predators can't reach them.
So, could you nap upside down like a bat?
key_facts: Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight
Bat wings can't generate enough lift from a standstill on the ground, and their hind legs are too small and light to run for a takeoff
Hanging lets them simply let go and drop into flight
Tendons in the feet are pulled tight by the bat's body weight, closing the claws with no muscle effort; muscles are needed to open them
Bats are light enough that blood pooling in the head is not a problem
Roosting high keeps them out of reach of most predators
Some species like the little brown bat sleep around 19-20 hours a day
